text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert CI-NET-ALB-01 fired -> high TLS handshake failures observed from edge ALB in us-west-2. Error rate spike started ~10m ago. Auto-escalation window 3m. Runbook: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/alb-tls-handshake

pagerduty: Incident triggered by alerting rule: alb_tls_handshake_rate > 5% for 5m (threshold: 2%). Affected: customer-facing endpoints (api.redwood.com) in us-west-2.

olga: acked. I'm on it. grabbing logs + starting triage. tagging @netops.

sam: noted. if it's certificate/SNI related we should consider weighted failover to us-east immediately. 

olga: quick check: ALB target health shows 2/6 targets Unhealthy in us-west-2 target-group tg-api-1. TLS failures: "alert: TLS handshake failure: ssl_alert_recv: handshake failure" in the LB logs. Backend pods are healthy. This looks like the ALB failing before reaching targets.

jordan: I'm seeing a cert mismatch in the ALB config history: change rolled 2h ago that added a new wildcard cert that doesn't include the customer-facing SAN we expect for api.redwood.com when SNI is present. Could be SNI mismatch for certain client cipher suites.

netops: confirming. Checking ACM cert versions and ALB listener rules now. If the listener uses the wrong cert for some ciphers it will handshake fail instead of routing.

olga: mitigation plan: 1) roll back to previous cert on the listener (hot rollback) 2) if rollback time >5m, start weighted DNS failover to us-east-1 for api.redwood.com 3) open incident page and notify CS for customer comms. I'll attempt (1) now.

sre-runner: runbook step executed: snapshot current listener config. Command: ```aws elbv2 describe-listeners --load-balancer-arn $ALB_ARN --region us-west-2```

olga: rolled listener cert back to cert-arn: arn:aws:acm:us-west-2:123456:certificate/old-cert-abc. Confirming metrics...

netops: health checks recovering on targets. TLS handshake failure rate dropped from 9% -> 0.7% in last 2m. Good signal.

pagerduty: auto-escalation cancelled.

sam: great. keep monitoring for 30m. We should still do RCA and validate cert deployment pipeline so a bad cert doesn't get promoted.

jordan: filing a post-incident ticket: PI-2026-042. Initial notes: bad cert promotion to prod ALB caused SNI mismatch for a subset of client ciphers leading to handshake failures, partial regional impact. Will include timeline + deploy audit.

olga: customer-impact: CS says 12 customers reported 5xx errors in us-west-2 in last 30m. No data corruption. Suggest reaching out to top-affected accounts with mitigation summary. @customer-success can you prepare a short note?

customer-success: on it. Drafting status update: "We've identified and rolled back a TLS cert change causing intermittent handshake failures for customers connecting to us-west-2. Traffic is restored; no action required. We'll follow up with RCA and preventive steps."

sam: follow-ups: 1) make cert promotion a canary + validation step that includes active TLS handshake tests across cipher suites 2) add an alert for sudden cert rotation on ALBs 3) document rollback playbook in runbooks.

olga: adding retention metrics to the incident page. Marking incident as mitigated. Will keep thread open for RCA edits. :white_check_mark:
